readings.title: David and Goliath
readings.subtitle: The Battle is YeHoVaH's
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:32] And Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “Let no man’s heart fall because of him, your servant is going to fight with this Philistine.” [33] And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are but a youth, and he a man of battle from his youth.” [34] And Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “Your servant has been keeping <dn>את</dn> his father’s sheep, and when a lion or a bear came and took a lamb out of the flock, [35] I went out after it and smote it, and delivered it from its mouth. And when it rose against me, I caught it by its beard, and smote it and killed it. [36] “Your servant has smitten both <dn>את</dn> lion and bear. And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, seeing he has defied the armies of the living <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [37] And Dawiḏ said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, <dn>He</dn> does deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.” And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ, “Go, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you!” [38] And Sha’ul dressed <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ with his garments and put a bronze helmet on his head, and put a coat of armor on him. [39] And Dawiḏ girded <dn>את</dn> his sword over his garments, and began to go, for he had not tried them. And Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “I am unable to go with these, for I have not tried them.” And Dawiḏ put them off him. [40] And he took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones from the stream, and put them in a shepherd’s bag, in a pouch which he had, and his sling was in his hand. And he drew near to the Philistine. [41] And the Philistine came, and began drawing near to Dawiḏ, and the man who bore the shield went before him. [42] And when the Philistine looked about and saw <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ, he despised him, for he was a youth, and ruddy and good looking. [43] And the Philistine said to Dawiḏ, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ by his mighty ones. [44] And the Philistine said to Dawiḏ, “Come to me, and I give <dn>את</dn> your flesh to the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field!” [45] And Dawiḏ said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin. But I come to you in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the armies of Yisra’el, whom you have defied. [46] “This day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall shut you up into my hand, and I shall smite you and take <dn>את</dn> your head from you, and give <dn>את</dn> the carcasses of the camp of the Philistines today to the birds of the heavens and the wild beasts of the earth, so that all the earth know that there is an <dn>Elohim</dn> for Yisra’el, [47] and all this assembly know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not save with sword and spear, for the battle belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> shall give you into our hands.” [48] And it came to be, when the Philistine rose and came and drew near to meet Dawiḏ, that Dawiḏ hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine. [49] And Dawiḏ put <dn>את</dn> his hand in his bag and took out a stone, and slung it and smote <dn>את</dn> the Philistine in his forehead, so that the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth. [50] Thus Dawiḏ prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone, and smote <dn>את</dn> the Philistine and killed him. And there was no sword in the hand of Dawiḏ. [51] Then Dawiḏ ran and stood over the Philistine, and took <dn>את</dn> his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off <dn>את</dn> his head with it.

readings.title: Victory and Introduction
readings.subtitle: David Before Saul
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:51b] And when the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled. [52] And the men of Yisra’el and Yehuḏah rose up and shouted, and pursued <dn>את</dn> the Philistines as far as the entrance of the valley and to the gates of Eqron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell along the way to Shaʽarayim, even as far as Gath and Eqron. [53] And the children of Yisra’el returned from chasing the Philistines, and they plundered <dn>את</dn> their camps. [54] And Dawiḏ took <dn>את</dn> the head of the Philistine and brought it to Yerushalayim, but he put <dn>את</dn> his weapons in his tent. [55] And when Sha’ul saw <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ going out against the Philistine, he said to Aḇněr, the commander of the army, “Aḇněr, whose son is this youth?” And Aḇněr said, “As your soul lives, O sovereign, I do not know.” [56] And the sovereign said, “Inquire whose son this young man is.” [57] And as Dawiḏ returned from smiting the Philistine, Aḇněr took him and brought him before Sha’ul with the head of the Philistine in his hand. [58] And Sha’ul said to him, “Whose son are you, young man?” And Dawiḏ answered, “The son of your servant Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite.”

readings.title: Saul's Jealousy
readings.subtitle: The Women's Song
readings.text: [1 Samuel 18:1] And it came to be, when he had ceased speaking to Sha’ul, that the soul of Yonathan was knit to the soul of Dawiḏ, and Yonathan loved him as his own soul. [2] And Sha’ul took him that day, and would not let him return to his father’s house. [3] And Yonathan and Dawiḏ made a covenant, because he loved <dn>את</dn> him as his own soul. [4] And Yonathan took off <dn>את</dn> the robe that was on him and gave it to Dawiḏ, and <dn>את</dn> his garments, even to his sword and his bow and his belt. [5] And Dawiḏ went out wherever Sha’ul sent him, and he acted wisely. And Sha’ul set him over the men of war, and it was right in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of Sha’ul’s servants. [6] And it came to be as they came in, as Dawiḏ returned from smiting <dn>את</dn> the Philistine, that the women came out from all the cities of Yisra’el, singing and dancing, to meet Sha’ul the sovereign, with tambourines, with joy, and with musical instruments. [7] And the women sang as they danced, and said, “Sha’ul has smitten his thousands, and Dawiḏ his ten thousands.” [8] And Sha’ul was very wroth, and this matter was evil in his eyes, and he said, “They have given Dawiḏ ten thousands, and to me they have given thousands. And what more for him but the reign?” [9] And Sha’ul looked at <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ with suspicion from that day forward. [10] And it came to be on the next day that an evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon Sha’ul, and he prophesied inside the house, while Dawiḏ played music with his hand, as at other times. And there was a spear in Sha’ul’s hand. [11] And Sha’ul hurled <dn>את</dn> the spear, for he said, “I smite Dawiḏ even to the wall.” But Dawiḏ withdrew from his presence twice. [12] And Sha’ul was afraid of Dawiḏ, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with him, but had turned aside from Sha’ul. [13] So Sha’ul removed him from his presence, and made him his commander of a thousand. And he went out and came in before the people. [14] And Dawiḏ was acting wisely in all his ways, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with him. [15] And Sha’ul saw that he was acting very wisely, and he was afraid of him. [16] But all Yisra’el and Yehuḏah loved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ, for he went out and came in before them.

readings.title: The Price of a Bride
readings.subtitle: Saul's Trap for David
readings.text: [1 Samuel 18:17] And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ, “Look, my older daughter Měraḇ! I give her to you as a wife. Only be brave for me, and fight the battles of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” For Sha’ul thought, “Let not my hand be against him, but let the hand of the Philistines be against him.” [18] And Dawiḏ said to Sha’ul, “Who am I, and what is my life or my father’s family in Yisra’el, that I should be son-in-law to the sovereign?” [19] But it came to be at the time when Měraḇ, Sha’ul’s daughter, should have been given to Dawiḏ, that she was given to Aḏri’ěl the Meḥolathite as a wife. [20] And Miḵal, Sha’ul’s daughter, loved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ. And they told Sha’ul, and the matter was right in his eyes. [21] And Sha’ul said, “I give her to him, that she might be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines might be against him.” And Sha’ul said to Dawiḏ a second time, “You become my son-in-law today.” [22] And Sha’ul commanded <dn>את</dn> his servants, “Speak to Dawiḏ secretly, saying, ‘Look, the sovereign delights in you, and all his servants love you. And now, be the sovereign’s son-in-law.’ ” [23] And Sha’ul’s servants spoke <dn>את</dn> those words in the hearing of Dawiḏ. And Dawiḏ said, “Does it seem light in your eyes to be a sovereign’s son-in-law, seeing I am a poor and lightly esteemed man?” [24] And the servants of Sha’ul reported to him, saying, “Dawiḏ has spoken according to these words.” [25] And Sha’ul said, “Say this to Dawiḏ, ‘The sovereign has no delight in any payment for the bride, but in one hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to take vengeance on the sovereign’s enemies.’ ” But Sha’ul thought to cause Dawiḏ to fall by the hand of the Philistines. [26] And his servants declared <dn>את</dn> these words to Dawiḏ, and it pleased Dawiḏ well to become the sovereign’s son-in-law. And the days had not expired, [27] when Dawiḏ and his men arose and went and smote two hundred men of the Philistines. And Dawiḏ brought <dn>את</dn> their foreskins, and they gave them in full to the sovereign, to become the sovereign’s son-in-law. Then Sha’ul gave him Miḵal his daughter as a wife. [28] And Sha’ul saw and knew that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with Dawiḏ, and that Miḵal, Sha’ul’s daughter, loved him. [29] And Sha’ul was still more afraid of Dawiḏ. So Sha’ul became an enemy of Dawiḏ all the days. [30] And the commanders of the Philistines went out to fight. And it came to be, whenever they went out, that Dawiḏ acted more wisely than all the servants of Sha’ul, so that his name was highly influential.

readings.title: Jonathan's Intercession
readings.subtitle: Saul Tries to Kill David Again
readings.text: [1 Samuel 19:1] And Sha’ul spoke to Yonathan his son and to all his servants, to kill <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ. But Yonathan, Sha’ul’s son, delighted much in Dawiḏ. [2] And Yonathan reported to Dawiḏ, saying, “My father Sha’ul seeks to kill you. And now, please be on guard in the morning, and you shall dwell in secrecy and hide yourself. [3] “And let me go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and speak with my father about you. And I shall see what comes of it and report to you.” [4] And Yonathan spoke well of <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ to Sha’ul his father, and said to him, “Let not the sovereign sin against his servant, against Dawiḏ, because he has not sinned against you, and because his works have been very good toward you. [5] “For he took <dn>את</dn> his life in his hands and smote <dn>את</dn> the Philistine, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> worked a great deliverance for all Yisra’el. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then do you sin against innocent blood, to kill <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ without cause?” [6] And Sha’ul listened to the voice of Yonathan, and Sha’ul swore, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, he does not die.” [7] And Yonathan called Dawiḏ, and Yonathan reported to him <dn>את</dn> all these words. So Yonathan brought <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ to Sha’ul, and he was in his presence as beforehand. [8] And there was fighting again, and Dawiḏ went out and fought with the Philistines, and smote them with a great slaughter, and they fled from before him. [9] And the evil spirit from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was upon Sha’ul as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand. And Dawiḏ was playing the lyre with his hand. [10] And Sha’ul sought to smite the spear through Dawiḏ, and into the wall, but he slipped away from the presence of Sha’ul, so he smote <dn>את</dn> the spear into the wall. And Dawiḏ fled and escaped that night.

readings.title: The Escape through the Window
readings.subtitle: Michal Deceives Saul's Messengers
readings.text: [1 Samuel 19:11] And Sha’ul sent messengers to Dawiḏ’s house to watch him and to kill him in the morning. And Miḵal, Dawiḏ’s wife, reported to him, saying, “If you do not save <dn>את</dn> your life tonight, tomorrow you are killed.” [12] So Miḵal let <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ down through a window. And he went and fled and escaped. [13] And Miḵal took <dn>את</dn> the household idol and laid it in the bed, and put a cover of goats’ hair for his head, and covered it with clothes. [14] And when Sha’ul sent messengers to take <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ, she said, “He is sick.” [15] Then Sha’ul sent the messengers back to see <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ, saying, “Bring him up to me in the bed, to put him to death.” [16] And the messengers came in and saw the household idol was in the bed, with a cover of goats’ hair for his head. [17] And Sha’ul said to Miḵal, “Why have you deceived me like this, and sent <dn>את</dn> my enemy away, so that he has escaped?” And Miḵal answered Sha’ul, "He said to me, ‘Let me go! Why should I kill you?’ "

readings.title: Saul among the Prophets
readings.subtitle: David Flees to Ramah
readings.text: [1 Samuel 19:18] And Dawiḏ fled and escaped, and went to Shemu’el at Ramah, and told him <dn>את</dn> all that Sha’ul had done to him. And he and Shemu’el went and dwelt in Nayoth. [19] And it was reported to Sha’ul, saying, “See, Dawiḏ is at Nayoth in Ramah.” [20] And Sha’ul sent messengers to take <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ. And when they saw <dn>את</dn> the company of prophets prophesying, and Shemu’el standing as leader over them, the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon the messengers of Sha’ul, and they also prophesied. [21] And when Sha’ul was told, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied likewise. And Sha’ul sent messengers again the third time, and they prophesied also. [22] And he also went to Ramah, and came to the great well that is at Seku. And he asked and said, “Where are Shemu’el and Dawiḏ?” And one said, “Look, at Nayoth in Ramah.” [23] And he went there to Nayoth in Ramah. And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon him also, and he went on and prophesied until he came to Nayoth in Ramah. [24] And he also stripped off his garments and prophesied before Shemu’el as well, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, “Is Sha’ul also among the prophets?”

readings.title: Deliver Me from My Enemies
readings.subtitle: A Miktam of David when Saul Sent Men to Watch His House
readings.text: [Psalm 59:1] Deliver me from my enemies, O <dn>my Elohim</dn>; Set me on high from those who rise up against me. [2] Deliver me from workers of wickedness, And save me from men of blood. [3] For look, they have lain in wait for my life; The strong gather against me, Not for my transgression nor for my sin, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn. [4] Without my guilt, they run and prepare themselves. Awake to help me, and see! [5] And <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of hosts, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, Awake to punish all the gentiles; Do not show favor to any wicked traitors. Selah. [6] They return at evening, They growl like a dog, And go all around the city. [7] Look, they spew with their mouth; Swords are in their lips, For they say, “Who hears?” [8] But <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, laugh at them; <dn>You</dn> mock all the gentiles. [9] O my Strength, I wait for <dn>You</dn>; For <dn>Elohim</dn> is my strong tower. [10] <dn>My Elohim</dn> of kindness meets me; <dn>Elohim</dn> lets me look upon my adversaries. [11] Do not kill them, lest my people forget; Scatter them by <dn>Your</dn> power, And bring them down, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our shield. [12] For the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips, Let them even be caught in their pride, And for the cursing and lying which they speak. [13] Consume them in wrath, consume them, That they be no more; And let them know that <dn>Elohim</dn> is ruling in Yaʽaqoḇ To the ends of the earth. Selah. [14] And at evening they return, They growl like a dog, And go all around the city. [15] They wander up and down for food, And whine if they are not satisfied. [16] But I sing of <dn>Your</dn> power; And in the morning I sing aloud of <dn>Your</dn> kindness; For <dn>You</dn> have been my strong tower And a refuge in the day of my distress. [17] O my Strength, to <dn>You</dn> I sing praises; For <dn>Elohim</dn> is my strong tower, <dn>My Elohim</dn> of kindness.
